summary: Run the native Sage agent (ohf-sage.md + full corpus grep) as a PR reviewer over the same 6 held-out diffs, apples-to-apples vs the Copilot skill

findings.issue: provider.py wraps every parse loop (search, get_album_tracks, get_playlist_tracks, get_artist_albums, get_artist_toptracks, and all get_library_* generators) in `except Exception as err: self.logger.debug(...)` and continues. This is both a broad/bare-except violation and silent error-swallowing at debug level, hiding real bugs and malformed data.
findings.principle: MUST catch specific, expected exception types — no broad or bare except; and MUST never silently swallow errors or anomalous data (don't collapse failures into a debug log and continue).

findings.issue: get_config_entries() hardcodes every user-facing label and description ('You are authenticated with Yandex Music', 'Audio quality', 'Reset authentication', the multi-step token instructions, etc.) directly in ConfigEntry objects, and no strings.json ships with the provider. The pre-commit hook fails when a ConfigEntry hardcodes label/description text instead of using strings.json.
findings.principle: MUST route all user-facing labels, descriptions, and typed error messages through strings.json / a translation_key (English source), never hardcoding display text.

findings.issue: Private methods are placed above public ones: api_client.py defines `_ensure_connected` before the public library/search/get methods, and provider.py defines `_get_provider_item_id` above the public `get_stream_details`. The pre-commit hook fails when a class puts a public/dunder method below a private one.
findings.principle: MUST order file/class contents public (and dunder) methods first, private/helper methods at the bottom.

findings.issue: YandexMusicClient constructs `ClientAsync(self._token).init()`, which creates and owns its own aiohttp ClientSession per provider instance rather than reusing the shared global session. Providers must never spin up their own ClientSession; external HTTP should go through self.mass.http_session.
findings.principle: MUST reuse the shared global aiohttp session (self.mass.http_session); never create a new ClientSession per request or per provider.

findings.issue: api_client single-item/streaming methods (get_track, get_tracks, get_album, get_playlist, get_track_download_info, and every like_/unlike_ method) catch NetworkError/BadRequestError and collapse them into None, [], or False. A transient network failure becomes indistinguishable from 'not found' (streaming then raises MediaNotFoundError for what was really a network error), and library edits silently report False on API failure.
findings.principle: MUST never silently swallow errors — let it propagate or raise; don't collapse failures into a bool, None, or a silent default (raise from MA's typed exception hierarchy instead).

findings.issue: streaming.py _get_content_type() defaults any unknown codec to ContentType.MP3, and get_stream_details puts that guessed content_type on the StreamDetails audio_format that drives playback. A wrong-but-plausible codec on streamdetails can corrupt the playback pipeline; unknown codecs should be ContentType.UNKNOWN, not guessed.
findings.principle: MUST keep StreamDetails audio-quality fields (codec, bit depth, sample rate) accurate since they drive playback — set ContentType.UNKNOWN rather than guess wrong.

findings.issue: The provider decorates get_artist/get_album/get_track/get_playlist (single media-item lookups) with @use_cache. External-API lookups may use @use_cache, but caching the parsed media items themselves is the core controllers' job — providers shouldn't cache media items, which risks double-caching and stale-item bugs. Reserve provider-level @use_cache for raw external lookups.
findings.principle: MUST route external-API lookups through MA's cache with a per-method TTL; providers don't hand-roll caching and don't cache media items themselves (the core controllers own that).

findings.issue: The 'Audio quality' (High/Lossless) selector is exposed as a user-facing config option. MA prefers a sane default (or auto-selecting the best available quality the account supports) over adding a toggle; question whether this option is needed rather than defaulting to a config entry.
findings.principle: Prefer sane defaults over user-facing config options; question whether each toggle is needed.

findings.issue: constants.py declares several symbols with no consumer in the diff (CONF_ACTION_AUTH, LABEL_TOKEN, LABEL_AUTH_INSTRUCTIONS, IMAGE_SIZE_SMALL, IMAGE_SIZE_MEDIUM, CACHE_TTL_ARTIST/ALBUM/PLAYLIST). Speculative/unused scaffolding should be dropped in favor of the simplest code the provider actually uses.
findings.principle: Prefer the simplest solution that works and avoid speculative flexibility / abstractions with no real consumer.

review.verdict: Won't be accepted as-is: a solid new Yandex Music provider, but it trips three hard/enforced MUSTs (broad-except-and-swallow across every parse loop, hardcoded ConfigEntry labels instead of strings.json, and private-above-public method ordering) plus per-provider aiohttp session creation, error-collapsing in the API client, and streamdetails codec guessing that must be fixed before merge.

A well-structured new Samsung WAM player provider, but not accepted as-is: it has MUST violations (broad exception catching, an unmanaged fire-and-forget task) plus several should-fix issues (always-on polling, reaching into pywam internals, a hacky log-suppression workaround, single-consumer over-abstraction, and a placeholder manifest documentation URL).

findings.issue: `_setup_player` (except Exception as err) and `_periodic_probe_task` (except Exception as err) catch bare/broad Exception. `_setup_player` also merely logs a warning and returns, so any real setup bug is caught and effectively swallowed rather than surfaced.
findings.principle: MUST catch specific, expected exception types — no broad/bare except, which hides real bugs; and MUST never silently swallow errors.

findings.issue: `on_config_updated` fires `self.mass.create_task(self.device_config.set_name(new_name))` with no stored reference, no tracking/cancel on unload, and no done-callback, so any exception from the rename command is silently lost.
findings.principle: MUST manage background asyncio tasks: keep a reference to create_task, track and cancel on unload, and give a done-callback so failures surface.

findings.issue: WamPlayer sets `_attr_needs_poll = True` with a fixed 30s `_attr_poll_interval` and runs a health-check poll unconditionally, even though it already subscribes to pywam speaker events. Hardware is polled at all times, not only while actively playing.
findings.principle: MUST stay event-driven — rely on events/announcements and poll hardware adaptively only when actively playing.

findings.issue: `create_speaker_attributes` reads `raw._playstatus`, a private attribute of the pywam library object, and `state_sync/handler.py` monkey-patches `speaker.events.event_SpeakerStatus`. Both depend on brittle library internals that can break on any pywam update.
findings.principle: Do not reach into a dependency's private attributes/internals directly — maintainers repeatedly reject this as brittle.

findings.issue: `setup()` suppresses SpeakerStatus log spam by installing a global logging.Filter on the `pywam.events` logger, calling setLevel on several third-party loggers, and (in state_sync) monkey-patching the event handler — a workaround layered three ways instead of addressing the noise at its source or via normal log configuration.
findings.principle: MUST fix a problem at its root cause, not with a hacky workaround.

findings.issue: Each command family is a separate handler class in its own file over shared base classes — e.g. VolumeHandler (two one-line methods) and DeviceConfigHandler (a single set_name method). This adds indirection for logic with only one real consumer.
findings.principle: Prefer not introducing an abstraction (helper class, separate file) for logic with only one real consumer; keep the solution simple and avoid speculative structure.

findings.issue: The manifest ships with `"documentation": "URL_TO_DOCUMENTATION"`, an unfilled placeholder rather than a real documentation URL.
findings.principle: MUST have every provider manifest.json declare its mandatory keys and stay internally consistent (mechanically enforced).

findings.issue: The provider hand-rolls timing/retry logic: `retry_command` does its own asyncio.sleep exponential backoff, discovery's `_periodic_probe_task` is a raw `while ... asyncio.sleep(PROBE_INTERVAL)` loop, and `player.await_state_change` reimplements a wait-for-condition helper.
findings.principle: Prefer the built-in task scheduler (mass.call_later), the built-in debouncer, and wait_for_state helpers over hand-rolled timers/sleep loops.

findings.issue: Several methods use nested if/else where an early guard/return would be clearer, e.g. `on_config_updated` (nested `if new_name:` / `if self.connected:`) and discovery's `handle_discovery_event`.
findings.principle: Prefer early guard clauses / returns over nested if/else blocks.

findings.issue: The new _session_established() method logs with f-strings: logger.info(f"Streaming session established in {self._session_establishment_ms}ms...") and logger.warning(f"Configured value of {...}..."). MA requires %s-style positional logging arguments, never f-strings, inside logger calls. (These lines also exceed the enforced Ruff line-length of 100.)
findings.principle: MUST use %s-style positional logging arguments, not f-strings, inside logger calls.

findings.issue: Bare string-literals are used as comments rather than # comments: inside the `if self._connected_ts is not None:` guard sits `"""We have previously connected, so we ignore this call"""` as a no-op statement. Comments should use # and explain complex blocks; a non-docstring string statement will also trip Ruff (select=["ALL"], B018 useless-expression).
findings.principle: MUST write caller-facing docstrings and only use # comments to explain complex multi-line blocks describing current behavior; pass Ruff with select=["ALL"].

findings.issue: The reworked ConfigEntry for CONF_SESSION_ESTABLISHMENT_LATENCY hardcodes its label ("Expected milliseconds to establish streaming session...") and multi-line description directly instead of routing them through strings.json / a translation_key. The AirPlay2 ALERT ConfigEntry label is likewise hardcoded. This is an enforced pre-commit rule (pre-existing pattern in this provider, but the change edits these exact strings).
findings.principle: MUST route all user-facing labels, descriptions, and typed error messages through strings.json / a translation_key, never hardcoding display text.

findings.issue: The change introduces a user-tunable session_establishment_latency knob as an admitted interim band-aid for a not-understood AirPlay2 timing/sync problem (docstrings say "The exact reasoning for this is not yet understood and it seems counter intuitive" and "It will be removed when a robust synchronisation method is implemented"). This tunes around the symptom rather than fixing the root cause in the AirPlay2 binary / timing layer.
findings.principle: MUST fix a problem at its root cause and correct owning location, not with a workaround.

findings.issue: _recommended_session_establishment_latency() encodes empirically-derived magic offsets (high rounded up to nearest 100, low = high-600) whose logic the author states is not understood and counter-intuitive, then warns users when their config falls outside that window. This is complex, hard-to-maintain tuning heuristics exposed to end users; a sane fixed default (or no user knob) would be simpler.
findings.principle: Prefer the simplest solution that works and keep code simple/maintainable; prefer sane defaults over user-facing config options rather than exposing technical tuning knobs.

findings.issue: _log_cli_output strips a fixed 31-character prefix from every cliap2 stderr line (line[31:]) to remove the binary's timestamp/loglevel. This hardcoded slice silently corrupts log output if the bundled binary's log format width ever changes (the binaries are updated in this same PR).
findings.principle: Prefer the simplest robust solution and avoid brittle hardcoded assumptions; keep AI-assisted code simple and human-maintainable.

review.verdict: Needs changes before it would be accepted: one hard MUST violation (f-string logging), plus a root-cause concern (an admittedly-interim latency knob tuning around an unresolved AirPlay2 timing bug), hardcoded ConfigEntry label/description that should live in strings.json, and a string-literal-as-comment that also risks the Ruff ALL gate.
Acceptable and single-purpose, but fix the unguarded source_obj.titles["primary"] dict access (KeyError risk) before merge.

findings.issue: The `elif source_obj.titles:` branch does `title = source_obj.titles["primary"]`, a direct dict-key access guarded only by the dict's truthiness. A non-empty `titles` dict that lacks a "primary" key raises KeyError, crashing get_stream_details. Use `source_obj.titles.get("primary", "")` (or validate the key exists).
findings.principle: Guard direct dict-key access that depends on external/provider-shaped data; check the key exists or use .get() with a fallback to prevent KeyErrors.

findings.issue: The new title chain treats `episode.metadata` as possibly None (`elif episode.metadata and episode.metadata.description:`), but the following line `if episode.metadata.images:` still dereferences `episode.metadata` unconditionally, which would AttributeError when metadata is None. The crashing line is pre-existing/adjacent, but the change now assumes metadata can be None on this path, so the two should be consistent (guard the images access too).
findings.principle: Guard for empty/missing state before dereferencing rather than letting it crash; the change itself introduces the None assumption, so keep the adjacent access consistent.

review.verdict: Mergeable AirPlay bug-fix (combine pairing flags, protocol fallback, interface resolution), but before merge: swap the Python built-in RuntimeError/TypeError raises for MA typed exceptions (or keep them as type-checker asserts), and add a log to the two silent exception suppressions so malformed data isn't dropped unnoticed.

findings.issue: The former type-checker asserts were replaced with Python built-in exceptions: `raise RuntimeError(...)` for missing airplay_discovery_info and `raise TypeError(...)` for a bad sync_adjust (and `raise RuntimeError` for missing raop_discovery_info in raop.py). MA requires failures to be raised from its own typed exception hierarchy, not Python built-ins.
findings.principle: MUST raise from MA's own typed exception hierarchy (SetupFailedError, ProviderUnavailableError, MediaNotFoundError, ...) rather than Python built-in exceptions.

findings.issue: The lines removed here (and in airplay2.py) were `assert ... is not None  # for type checker` guards. If these conditions are truly unreachable type-checker guards, MA's idiom is to keep them as a plain `assert ... # guard for type checker` rather than converting them to runtime raises; if they are genuinely reachable, they should raise a typed MA exception. Either way, built-in RuntimeError/TypeError is the wrong choice.
findings.principle: MA convention: use `assert X is not None  # guard for type checker` for pure type-checker invariants (marcelveldt review precedent).

findings.issue: In `_get_flags`, `contextlib.suppress(ValueError, TypeError)` silently drops a malformed `sf`/`flags` value and contributes 0 to the OR. The method's own comment notes that missing a source 'misses the pairing requirement', so silently zeroing a malformed source could cause MA to skip a required pairing without any trace. Suppressing specific exceptions is accepted MA style, but log the anomalous value at debug rather than swallowing it entirely.
findings.principle: MUST never silently swallow anomalous data into a silent default; let it surface (here: at least log it).

findings.issue: `_routing_lookup` catches `OSError` with a bare `pass` and returns an empty string. The routing probe failing is exactly the case worth a debug log before falling through to publish_ip/bind_ip; swallowing it with no trace makes interface-selection problems hard to diagnose.
findings.principle: MUST never silently swallow errors; log/surface them instead of a bare pass into a default.

findings.issue: handle_async_init creates a brand-new `aiohttp.ClientSession()` (line 117) and hands it to IBroadcastClient instead of reusing the shared `self.mass.http_session`. It is also opened in an `async with` block, so the session is closed the moment init returns while `self._client` keeps using it.
findings.principle: MUST reuse the shared global aiohttp session (self.mass.http_session); never create a new ClientSession per request or per provider.

findings.issue: Per-item API calls inside listing loops (N+1). `_get_tracks` (lines 260-270) calls `get_track` for every id in an album/playlist; `_parse_track` (lines 405-449) calls `get_artist` per artist and `get_album` per track; `_parse_album` (lines 340-357) fetches the artist and artwork per album while iterating `get_library_albums`. Iterating any listing fans out to one API call per element.
findings.principle: MUST never make a per-item API/DB call inside a loop over a listing (N+1); batch, reuse already-fetched data, or asyncio.gather independent calls.

findings.issue: The ConfigEntry definitions hardcode `label="Username"` and `label="Password"` (lines 96-97, 102-103) instead of routing display text through strings.json / a translation_key. No strings.json ships with the provider. This is mechanically checked and will fail pre-commit CI.
findings.principle: MUST route all user-facing labels, descriptions, and typed error messages through strings.json / a translation_key; never hardcode display text (ConfigEntry label/description).

findings.issue: get_playlist (lines 219-226) catches parse failures, logs at debug, then falls through to `return playlist` — but `playlist` is never assigned on the failure path, so it swallows the real error and raises an UnboundLocalError instead of propagating a typed error. Separately, get_library_tracks (line 193) catches IndexError and silently `continue`s with no logging.
findings.principle: MUST never silently swallow errors or anomalous data — let it propagate or raise; don't collapse failures into a bool, None, or a silent default.

findings.issue: get_stream_details hardcodes `content_type=ContentType.MPEG` for every track (lines 253-255), and the album/track ProviderMappings do the same (lines 318, 384-386). iBroadcast stores users' own uploaded files (which can be FLAC/ALAC/etc.), so this guesses the codec rather than reflecting it — StreamDetails audio-quality fields drive playback and must be accurate.
findings.principle: MUST keep StreamDetails audio-quality fields (codec, bit depth, sample rate) accurate since they drive playback — set ContentType.UNKNOWN rather than guess wrong.

findings.issue: get_artist_albums (line 167) does `albums.append(self._parse_album(album))` with no `await` — `_parse_album` is a coroutine, so the list is filled with un-awaited coroutine objects rather than Album instances (and the surrounding try/except can never catch a parse error because nothing is executed). Marcel has fixed this exact append-without-await pattern in review before.
findings.principle: Review-history precedent: maintainer corrected `result.artists.append(item)` to `append(await self._parse_artist(item))` — nested parse calls must be awaited before appending.

findings.issue: _parse_album (lines 343-344) calls `await self._client.get_artist(album_obj["artist_id"])` twice in a single expression (once for the value, once for the truthiness guard), doubling the API round-trips. Fetch once into a local and reuse it.
findings.principle: MUST never make redundant per-item API calls; reuse already-fetched data instead of re-calling the API.

findings.issue: Docstrings are one-line summaries without Sphinx `:param:` syntax; the server repo mandates Sphinx-style docstrings with the summary on its own next line and `:param:` for arguments (e.g. get_config_entries documents its params in prose rather than `:param:` form).
findings.principle: MUST write Sphinx-style docstrings with :param: syntax; no Google-style or bullet-style.

review.verdict: Won't be accepted as-is: a new iBroadcast provider with four MUST-level violations — creating its own aiohttp ClientSession instead of self.mass.http_session, pervasive N+1 API calls in listing loops, hardcoded ConfigEntry labels (will fail CI), and error-swallowing — plus inaccurate hardcoded StreamDetails codec and a missing-await bug.
